summary: Phase 149O.20L.7G -- DeploymentBinding Producer Contract/Schema Evolution and Implementation Planning. Contract/schema-evolution and implementation-planning only -- no producer implemented, no DeploymentBinding created, no repository identity created on Dell, no Dell mutation, no election initiated. Independently re-derived every load-bearing 7F claim directly against current production source/contract text before building on it (none found wrong); discovered two additional findings 7F did not name: HMIC-001's 12-step validation algorithm (HMIC-REQ-103) never re-checks a live DeploymentBinding's status at validation time (F3-residual, deferred, non-blocking, out of scope for an HBDC-001-only amendment), and hatp_bootstrap.py's timestamp parser is deliberately looser than the 149O.1H-hardened strict grammar (deferred, non-blocking; a future producer's own output is bound to the strict grammar regardless via the new HBDC-REQ-067). Selected HBDC-001 v1.0 -> v1.1 in-place amendment over a dedicated new contract as the normative home: HBDC-001 already owns DeploymentBinding's authority semantics (section 16) and is already one of HMIC-001's 28 digest-participating bound-contract files, so the new text is automatically digest-bound with no separate future HMIC amendment required -- mirroring this repository's own amend-in-place convention already demonstrated by HMIC-001's own four prior amendment waves. Added HBDC-REQ-056 through HBDC-REQ-070 (15 new requirements covering writer non-agent-reachability, read-only field derivation matching HMIC-REQ-045's discipline, admin-enrollment-context inputs, idempotent-preserve creation with fail-closed conflict handling, explicit rotate/revoke as distinct operations from creation, revocation-as-field-mutation/rotation-as-in-place-overwrite with no trust-store history, mandatory audit-evidence emission into existing governance infrastructure, atomic-write-idiom reuse, explicit fresh-election-evidence requirement, election-reference-as-metadata-not-cryptographic-verification, admin-OS-principal-only invocability, future-writer strict timestamp grammar, repository-identity non-gating by this section, non-satisfaction of any real CHGR election by contract text alone, and automatic implementation_scope_digest participation) plus security invariants CBD-9/CBD-10. Resolved Finding F3 (DeploymentBinding/CertificationRecord cross-consistency) normatively as value-derived consistency with no schema change to either record -- both already independently re-derive repository_id/canonical_deployment_root from the same underlying primitives (repository_identity.py, hatp_bootstrap.resolve_canonical_deployment_root) rather than one storing a reference/digest of the other, confirmed directly against HMIC-REQ-043/044/045's exact text. Resolved Finding F4 (rotation/revocation lifecycle) normatively as no schema change -- the existing closed active/revoked vocabulary and the registry parser's schema-enforced single-entry-per-repository_id constraint (independently reconfirmed by reading _parse_registry_document directly) are sufficient; revocation is in-place field mutation, rotation is in-place field overwrite, and history of prior field values is the explicit responsibility of this repository's existing governance/provenance/audit-record infrastructure, not new trust-store schema. Zero src/pcae/** files were modified -- the DeploymentBinding dataclass and its validators are byte-unchanged, confirming the no-schema-change conclusion is literally true at the code level, not merely narrative. Produced a full 14-step producer-responsibility plan, caller/authority-verification-boundary model, error/result taxonomy proposal, producer-consumer round-trip test plan, and adversarial test plan, all explicitly unimplemented. Ran the full repository-wide fast_green suite twice, isolated via git stash (this phase's changes removed vs. restored), to attribute this phase's exact regression effect: 37 new test failures, every single one a historical phase-specific 'HBDC-001 contract bytes/version unchanged since my own phase entry' pinning assertion broken by the intentional, in-scope v1.1 amendment -- exactly the same class of breakage HMIC-001's own four prior amendments already caused their own pinning tests, classified tests-require-migration per this phase's own charter, named explicitly rather than concealed, zero unexplained regressions (comm -23 diff of the two full failure lists is empty). Verdict: CONTRACT/SCHEMA EVOLUTION COMPLETE -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. HBDC-REQ-042 remains OPEN -- SOLE HBDC RESIDUAL, unchanged and not re-measured this phase (no Dell access occurred).
